plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 (24-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack) based on iteration_07 results showing best_target_score improvement from 0.601 to 0.691. Following feedback directive to test asymmetrical optimization: isolate whether performance margin stems from back-end phase adjustments or requires full-stack co-optimization. Three complementary routes proposed: (1) freeze front 12 layers, optimize back 12 with DE; (2) freeze back 12 layers, optimize front 12 with DE; (3) full-stack DE re-optimization with VIS-centered initialization to test wavelength-dependent convergence.

routes.title: Back-End Isolated DE Optimization on 24-Layer Dichroic Stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: The performance margin gained in iteration_07 (0.601 to 0.691) is primarily attributable to back-end layer phase adjustments; freezing layers 0-11 and optimizing only layers 12-23 should recover most of the achievable target score while reducing search dimensionality.
routes.design_principle: Asymmetrical optimization isolates contribution of back-end layers to dual-band spectral separation; DE optimizer with population=50, F=0.8, CR=0.9 provides global search capability for the 12 free variables.
routes.proposed_topology: 24-layer alternating stack: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate
design_variables: layers 0-11 frozen at iteration_07 best candidate values
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Alternating HfO2/SiO2 sequence preserved for deposition simplicity
theory_basis: Transfer-matrix method for coherent plane-wave multilayer interference
Quarter-wave stack theory for broadband reflectors
Gradient-based and evolutionary optimization for thin-film design
expected_advantages: Reduced search dimensionality (12 vs 24 variables) accelerates convergence
Isolates back-end layer contribution to spectral performance
Tests whether front-end layers are already near-optimal
known_risks: Freezing front layers may prevent discovery of better global solutions
DE may stagnate if back-end layers have limited influence on target bands
Performance may drop significantly if front-back coupling is strong
routes.execution_request_english: Execute TMM optimization for a 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack on fused silica substrate under normal incidence. Initialize all 24 layer thicknesses to iteration_07 best candidate values: [77.71, 177.76, 65.96, 87.63, 94.31, 100.73, 236.50, 85.64, 126.52, 87.80, 60.22, 87.68, 209.35, 88.73, 63.43, 79.31, 63.65, 84.16, 163.16, 212.54, 63.22, 82.93, 177.90, 68.43] nm. Freeze layers 0-11 at these values. Apply Differential Evolution optimizer (population=50, F=0.8, CR=0.9, max_generations=200) exclusively to layers 12-23 with bounds 50-280 nm. Evaluate coherent TMM at normal incidence for unpolarized light. Compute target score as weighted mean of (transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band) and (reflectance in 400-700 nm band) with equal weights. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, run_status, and final thicknesses_nm for all 24 layers. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Follows feedback directive to test asymmetrical optimization: freeze front 12 layers, optimize back 12 layers with DE to isolate whether performance margin stems from back-end phase adjustments.

routes.title: Front-End Isolated DE Optimization on 24-Layer Dichroic Stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: The front-end layers (0-11) contribute more significantly to visible-band reflectance than back-end layers; freezing layers 12-23 and optimizing only layers 0-11 should reveal whether front-end phase matching is the limiting factor for dual-band performance.
routes.design_principle: Complementary asymmetrical optimization tests the opposite hypothesis from route_02_refine_01; if both front-only and back-only optimization achieve similar scores, full-stack coupling is weak and sequential optimization is viable.

routes.title: VIS-Centered Quarter-Wave Initialization with Full-Stack DE Optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing from visible-band quarter-wave thicknesses (centered at 550 nm) rather than IR-centered values (1550 nm) will discover different local optima; full-stack DE optimization from this initialization may achieve comparable or better target scores than gradient-based IR-centered initialization.
routes.design_principle: Different initialization tests optimizer sensitivity to starting point; VIS-centered quarter-wave stack should provide high visible reflectance baseline, testing whether IR transmission can be recovered through DE search.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers)
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: VIS quarter-wave initialization: HfO2 ~95 nm, SiO2 ~145 nm at 550 nm center
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory: optical thickness = lambda_center / 4
Visible-band centered design prioritizes 400-700 nm reflectance
DE global optimizer can escape local optima from gradient-based methods
expected_advantages: VIS-centered start may achieve higher visible reflectance baseline
Full-stack optimization avoids asymmetrical freezing artifacts
known_risks: IR transmission may be harder to recover from VIS-centered start
DE on 24 variables may require more generations to converge
May not exceed iteration_07 score if IR-centered initialization is superior
